mainTopic: פיגול in a מנחה: the condition that the מתיר be offered כמצותו, and whether burning the קומץ can make lacking שירים פיגול
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה's rules of פיגול for a מנחה. If, during any of the four עבודות, the כהן intends to eat or burn the offering outside its place, it is פסול with no כרת. If he intends to do so after its time, it is פיגול with כרת. This holds only if the מתיר, the קומץ, was offered כמצותו, with no other wrong intent mixed in. A place-intent, or a שלא לשמן intent in a מנחת חוטא or מנחת קנאות, blocks פיגול. רבי יהודה says that when time and place intents are mixed, whichever came first decides, while חכמים say it is always just פסול. The גמרא then asks whether burning the קומץ can make שירים that became חסר into פיגול, and whether it takes them out of מעילה. רב הונא says no, because a חסרון is a flaw in the item itself. רבא says yes, because the שירים are still inside the עזרה. רבא begins a proof from רבי חייא's version of a משנה, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the previous ruling: it is פיגול and carries כרת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its earlier case by ruling that the offering is פיגול and one who eats it is חייב כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offering is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a sentence that began before this section. The משנה is finishing its ruling that a wrong intent about time makes the offering פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול is more severe than a regular פסול. It is not only unfit; a person who eats the leftovers is punished with כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the intent to eat or burn it after its proper time
A heavenly punishment of being 'cut off'
One is liable for it, meaning punished for eating it

phrases.english: It is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before, about intending to eat or burn the offering after its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling from the משנה text that came just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent beyond the time makes the מנחה פיגול, with כרת for eating it.

steps.title: The general rule: wrong place means unfit, wrong time means פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a כלל. During any of the four עבודות, intent to eat or burn outside the place makes the offering פסול without כרת. Intent outside the time makes it פיגול with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: whoever takes the handful, puts it in the vessel, carries it, or burns it, and intends to eat what is normally eaten or burn what is normally burned, if he intends to do it outside its place, the offering is unfit but there is no כרת. If he intends to do it outside its time, it is פיגול and there is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the whole topic in one general rule that covers all four steps of the מנחה service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of wrong intent are compared. Intent about place (חוץ למקומו) only makes the offering פסול. Intent about time (חוץ לזמנו) makes it פיגול with כרת. The intent counts only if it is the normal kind: eating what people eat (the leftovers) or burning what goes on the מזבח (the קומץ and לבונה).

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Putting the קומץ into a holy vessel
Something that is normally eaten
Outside its proper place
After its proper time
Unfit, but without the punishment of כרת

steps.whatToRemember: Wrong place gives פסול with no כרת. Wrong time gives פיגול with כרת.
steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds of intent ruin the offering. The difference is only whether eating it carries כרת, which happens only with פיגול (wrong time).

phrases.english: This is the rule:
Anyone who takes the handful, or places it in the vessel,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'or', is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: one who carries it, one who burns it,
intending to eat something that is normally eaten,
or to burn something that is normally burned,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: outside its place, it is unfit, and there is no karet for it;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – פִּיגּוּל וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: outside its time, it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the earlier specific rulings into one general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During any of the four עבודות, intent outside the place makes the offering פסול without כרת. Intent outside the time makes it פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: The condition: the permitting part must be offered properly
steps.stepSummary: פיגול happens only if the מתיר, the קומץ, was otherwise offered כמצותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Provided that the permitting part is offered according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the rule of פיגול. Time-intent creates פיגול only when the offering was otherwise done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ is called the מתיר because burning it is what permits the leftovers to be eaten. If something else disqualified the offering, such as an intent about place, the time-intent cannot make it פיגול. It stays a plain פסול with no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that, on condition that
The part that permits the rest of the offering (here, the קומץ)
According to its מצוה, done properly

steps.whyThisMatters: This condition explains why mixing a place-intent with a time-intent removes the כרת. The next steps are built on it.

phrases.english: provided that he offers the permitting part according to its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the פיגול half of the general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול with כרת applies only when the מתיר was offered כמצותו.

steps.title: What counts as offering it properly?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what it means for the מתיר to be offered כמצותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the permitting part offered according to its מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a clarifying question to set up a list of examples. It is preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition 'כמצותו' was stated in general terms. Now the משנה wants to show exactly which combinations of intent meet it.

keyTerms.meaning: How? In what way?
Was offered

phrases.english: How is the permitting part offered according to its מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the condition just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which cases count as the מתיר being offered כמצותו, so that פיגול applies.

steps.title: Examples where it was offered properly, so it is פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Three cases count as כמצותו: silence followed by time-intent, time-intent followed by silence, or time-intent throughout. In all three it is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took the handful in silence, then put it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it with intent beyond its time; or he took the handful with intent beyond its time, then put it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it in silence; or he took the handful, put it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it all with intent beyond its time, this is the case where the permitting part was offered according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question with three examples where the only wrong intent present is about time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing a step 'בשתיקה', with no special intent, does not spoil anything. So any mix of silence and time-intent counts as כמצותו and makes the offering פיגול. What matters is that no place-intent was mixed in.

keyTerms.meaning: He took the handful (קומץ) from the מנחה
In silence, with no special intent
He carried it to the מזבח
He burned it on the מזבח

phrases.english: If he took the handful in silence,

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן בִּכְלִי וְהוֹלִיךְ וְהִקְטִיר חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ;
phrases.english: and placed it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it with intent beyond its time;
or if he took the handful with intent beyond its time,
and placed it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it in silence;
or if he took the handful, placed it in the vessel,
carried it, and burned it, all with intent beyond its time,
this is the case where the permitting part was offered according to its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with examples.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the only wrong intent is about time, with or without steps done in silence, the מתיר counts as offered כמצותו and the offering is פיגול.

steps.title: What counts as not offering it properly?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks the opposite question: when is the מתיר not offered כמצותו?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the permitting part not offered according to its מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a second list, this time of cases that fail the condition. It is preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After showing what works, the משנה shows what breaks the condition. That tells us when there is no פיגול even though a time-intent was present.

keyTerms.meaning: Was not offered (properly)

phrases.english: How is the permitting part not offered according to its מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question in step 4, now asking about the opposite case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which cases mean the מתיר was not offered כמצותו, so that there is no פיגול.

steps.title: Examples where a place intent ruins it, so there is no פיגול
steps.stepSummary: If a place-intent appears in any step, mixed with time-intent or alone, the מתיר is not כמצותו. The offering is פסול but not פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took the handful with intent outside its place, then put it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it with intent beyond its time; or he took the handful with intent beyond its time, then put it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it with intent outside its place; or he took the handful, put it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it all with intent outside its place, this is the case where the permitting part was not offered according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists cases where a wrong intent about place shows up, so the time-intent cannot create פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A place-intent already makes the offering פסול. Once that happens, the מתיר is not 'proper', so any time-intent cannot add פיגול and כרת. This is true whether the place-intent comes first or after the time-intent.

keyTerms.meaning: This is (the case)

steps.whatToRemember: Any place-intent mixed into the עבודות blocks פיגול. The offering is only פסול, with no כרת.
steps.confusionAlert: In this ruling of the משנה, even when the time-intent came first and the place-intent came in a later step, there is still no פיגול. Don't confuse this with רבי יהודה in step 10, who makes the order of the thoughts matter.

phrases.english: If he took the handful with intent outside its place,

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן בִּכְלִי וְהוֹלִיךְ וְהִקְטִיר חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ,
phrases.english: and placed it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it with intent beyond its time,
or if he took the handful with intent beyond its time,

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן בִּכְלִי וְהוֹלִיךְ וְהִקְטִיר חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ,
phrases.english: and placed it in the vessel, carried it, and burned it with intent outside its place,
or if he took the handful, placed it in the vessel,
carried it, and burned it, all with intent outside its place,
this is the case where the permitting part was not offered according to its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 and completes the contrast with step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Any intent outside the place, in any of the עבודות, means the מתיר was not offered כמצותו, so there is no פיגול.

steps.title: Not for their sake in a sinner's or jealousy meal offering
steps.stepSummary: With a מנחת חוטא or מנחת קנאות, if any step is done שלא לשמן, even alongside a time-intent, the מתיר is not offered כמצותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone took the handful from a sinner's meal offering or a jealousy meal offering not for their sake, and did the other steps with a beyond-its-time intent, or the reverse, or did all the steps not for their sake, then the permitting part was not offered properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps answering its question about when the מתיר is not offered כמצותו. It adds one more kind of case: doing the steps שלא לשמן with these two special meal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a מנחת חוטא and a מנחת קנאות, doing a step שלא לשמן is itself a פסול. So once a שלא לשמן thought is in the picture, the מתיר was not offered properly. A time-intent in another step therefore cannot create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering a poor sinner brings in place of an animal חטאת
The 'jealousy' meal offering brought by a סוטה
Not for their sake: done with intent for a different kind of offering
The permitting part (here the קומץ) that allows the rest to be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with ordinary meal offerings. For most of them, שלא לשמן does not make them פסול. It is these two offerings, which are like a חטאת, where שלא לשמן ruins the offering.

phrases.english: The sinner's meal offering and the jealousy meal offering
phrases.notes: The 'jealousy' offering is the one a סוטה brings.

phrases.english: that one took their handful not for their sake,
placed it in a vessel, carried it,
and burned it with intent for beyond its time;
or that he took the handful with intent for beyond its time,
placed it in a vessel, carried it,
and burned it not for their sake;
or that he took the handful and placed it in a vessel
and carried it and burned it not for their sake —
this is a case where the permitting part was not offered according to its מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא וּמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת שֶׁקְּמָצָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second type of not-כמצותו case (שלא לשמן in special offerings) to the place-intent cases of step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When is the מתיר not offered כמצותו? (the question from step 6)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שלא לשמן intent in any step of a מנחת חוטא or מנחת קנאות means the מתיר was not offered כמצותו.

steps.title: Mixing outside and tomorrow in one intention
steps.stepSummary: An intent to eat a כזית (or half a כזית) outside and a כזית (or half) tomorrow, in either order, makes the offering פסול with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended to eat an olive-size outside and an olive-size tomorrow, or the reverse, or half an olive-size outside and half tomorrow, or the reverse, it is invalid but there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on a case where one thought mixes 'outside its place' and 'beyond its time' together. The ruling is פסול, but not פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a place-intent is mixed in, the offering is not כמצותו, so it cannot become פיגול. That holds whichever thought comes first. In the half-size cases, neither intent even reaches the full כזית on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size amount, the basic measure for eating
Outside its required place: a place-intent
Tomorrow, after its allowed time: a time-intent
Invalid offering
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.english: To eat an olive-size outside
and an olive-size tomorrow,
an olive-size tomorrow and an olive-size outside,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר,
phrases.english: half an olive-size outside and half an olive-size tomorrow,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: half an olive-size tomorrow and half an olive-size outside —
it is invalid, and there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the place-intent rule of step 7 to a single intention that mixes place and time, in any order and amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed place and time intents, in either order and even in half-size amounts, make the offering פסול without כרת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the first thought decides
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the time-intent came first it is פיגול with כרת, and if the place-intent came first it is פסול with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said, this is the rule: if the time thought came before the place thought, it is פיגול and one gets כרת for it. If the place thought came before the time thought, it is invalid and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the previous ruling. He says the order of the thoughts matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, once a time-intent comes first, the פיגול is already set, and a later place thought cannot undo it. But if the place thought comes first, it ruins the offering before the time thought arrives. This rejects step 9's view that order doesn't matter.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Intent about time (eating beyond its time)
Intent about place (eating outside its area)
Came first
An offering ruined by a time-intent; eating it brings כרת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: this is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם –
phrases.english: if the time intent came before the place intent —
it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן –
phrases.english: If the place intent came before the time intent —
it is invalid, and there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the blanket ruling of step 9 by making the order of the thoughts decisive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Time-intent first gives פיגול with כרת; place-intent first gives פסול without כרת.

steps.title: חכמים: order makes no difference
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say that in both orders the offering is פסול with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: in both this case and that case, it is invalid and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים answer רבי יהודה and reject his distinction. Either way, it is just פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, any place-intent mixed into the act means the מתיר was not offered כמצותו. That is enough to block פיגול, no matter which thought came first. This matches the ruling in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one: both cases

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת: רבי יהודה says whichever thought comes first decides. חכמים say any mix with a place-intent is only פסול, never פיגול.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וָזֶה פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: both this and that are invalid, and there is no כרת for it.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means both orders: time-thought first or place-thought first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's distinction from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever the order of the thoughts, a mix with a place-intent is פסול without כרת.

steps.title: Can burning make lacking leftovers פיגול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the שירים became lacking before the הקטרה, and the קומץ is still burned but the שירים may not be eaten, does a time-intent during the burning make them פיגול?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: according to the one who says that if the leftovers became less between taking the handful and burning it, the handful is still burned for them, and since we hold those leftovers may not be eaten, what is the law? Does the burning work to make them פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a question. It takes the view that the קומץ is still burned even after the שירים shrank, and asks whether the burning can then make those שירים פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the הקטרה both permits the שירים and, with a time-intent, makes them פיגול. Here the burning does not permit them, because they stay forbidden to eat. So the question is whether a burning that cannot permit can still set them as פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the Sages)
The leftover part of the meal offering that the כהנים eat
Taking the handful out of the meal offering
Burning the handful on the מזבח
We hold, as a settled rule
To fix them in the status of פיגול

steps.whyThisMatters: This tests whether פיגול depends on the burning actually permitting the שירים, or whether the act of burning is enough by itself.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
according to the one who says:
leftovers that became lacking
between taking the handful and burning it —
he still burns the handful on their account,
and we hold
that those leftovers are forbidden to eat,
what is the law: does the burning work for them
to fix them as פיגול?
phrases.notes: He means a case where the קומץ was burned with intent to eat these leftovers the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins a new inquiry about the פיגול rules, building on the idea that the מתיר's burning is what sets פיגול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a burning that does not permit the שירים can still make them פיגול.

steps.title: Does the burning also remove the lacking remainder from misuse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second part to its question: does the הקטרה remove the חסר שירים from the prohibition of מעילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does the burning take them out of the prohibition of מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the question it started in the last step. Besides asking about פיגול, it now also asks about מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once the קומץ is burned, the שירים may be eaten by the כהנים and are no longer under מעילה. Here the שירים are חסר and cannot be eaten. So the question is whether the הקטרה still has its usual effects on them, both פיגול and leaving מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of using or benefiting from הקדש (holy property)
To take them out / remove them
From the status of

phrases.english: And [does it] remove them from [the prohibition of] misuse?
phrases.notes: Round brackets show the usual printed spelling; square brackets give the corrected spelling of the same word. 'Them' means the שירים that are lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second part (מעילה) to the פיגול question in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הקטרה of the קומץ removes שירים that became חסר from the status of מעילה, just as it would for complete שירים.

steps.title: רב הונא: the burning does not work on a lacking remainder
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that even רבי עקיבא would agree that the הקטרה does not work on שירים that are חסר, because the flaw is in the item itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רבי עקיבא holds that זריקה works on meat that went out. Even so, that applies only to meat that went out, because the meat is still whole and is disqualified only by something outside it. But a lack is a flaw in the item itself, so the burning does not help it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question with a no. He shows that even the lenient opinion, רבי עקיבא, would not let the הקטרה work in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says the זריקה still works for meat that left the עזרה (יוצא), because the meat itself is fine; only its location is wrong. A חסרון is different, since the item itself is now missing part of it. So the הקטרה does not make the שירים פיגול and does not take them out of מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח; it permits the meat to be eaten
Meat of a קרבן that left the עזרה and became פסול
A lack; part of the item is missing
A disqualification in the item's own body
Because of an outside factor, not the item itself
Burning the קומץ on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources of the rule. רבי עקיבא's rule is about זריקה of blood for meat that went out. רב הונא is comparing it to the הקטרה of the קומץ for שירים that are חסר.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Even according to Rabbi Akiva, who says
"Sprinkling is effective for [meat] that went out,"
phrases.notes: He means the זריקה still takes such meat out of מעילה, even though the meat may not be eaten.

phrases.english: that applies [only] to [meat] that went out,
since it is still whole, as it was,
and it is disqualified because of something else;
but a lack,
which is a disqualification of its own body –
the burning does not help it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא אפילו לרבי עקיבא דאמר זריקה מועלת ליוצא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-part question of steps 12 and 13 with a no.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הקטרה does not work on שירים that are חסר. They do not become פיגול and do not leave מעילה, because a חסרון is a flaw in the item itself, unlike יוצא.

steps.title: רבא: on the contrary, the burning does work on a lacking remainder
steps.stepSummary: רבא turns רב הונא's argument around. Even רבי אליעזר would agree that the הקטרה works on שירים that are חסר, because they are still inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: On the contrary! רבי אליעזר holds that זריקה does not work on meat that went out. Even so, that applies only to meat that went out, because it is no longer inside. But שירים that are lacking are still inside, so the burning does help them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רב הונא and gives the opposite answer. He says the הקטרה does work on the חסר שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the key factor is location, not wholeness. רבי אליעזר's reason that זריקה fails for יוצא is that the meat is outside the עזרה, where the זריקה cannot reach it. The חסר שירים are still inside, so even רבי אליעזר would agree the הקטרה works. That means they can become פיגול and they leave מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the reverse is true
Inside the עזרה (Temple courtyard)
It is not there
Is effective / helps

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא says the הקטרה fails because a חסרון is a flaw in the item itself. רבא says it works because the שירים are still inside the עזרה. Each one argues 'even according to' the תנא who seems less likely to agree with him. רב הונא argues even by the lenient רבי עקיבא, and רבא argues even by the strict רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument decides whether שירים that became חסר before the הקטרה can become פיגול and whether they leave מעילה.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: On the contrary,
even according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says
"Sprinkling is not effective for [meat] that went out" –
that applies [only] to [meat] that went out, since it is not inside,
but a lacking [remainder], which is inside –
the burning does help it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבא אדרבה אפילו לרבי אליעזר דאמר אין זריקה מועלת ליוצא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's answer from step 14 and turns his reasoning around to reach the opposite result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both רב הונא's conclusion and the principle he used to reach it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא made the item's wholeness the deciding factor. רבא says the real factor is location: being inside or outside the עזרה. By that test, the חסר שירים qualify.

steps.title: רבא points to two versions of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets up his proof. Our משנה says 'to eat its שירים outside, or a כזית of its שירים outside.' רבי חייא's version leaves out 'or a כזית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? Because the משנה teaches: someone who takes the קומץ from a מנחה intending to eat its leftovers outside, or an olive-size of its leftovers outside. But רבי חייא teaches only 'someone who takes the קומץ from a מנחה' and does not say 'or an olive-size'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts proving his point from Step 15 by quoting our משנה next to רבי חייא's version of it. This step sets up the evidence, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the two versions is that רבי חייא leaves out the words 'or a כזית'. רבא is going to argue that this missing phrase tells us what kind of case רבי חייא had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? This is how a sage opens his own proof.
Taking the handful (קומץ) out of the מנחה
An olive-size, the smallest amount that counts as 'eating'
Outside the עזרה, where the שירים may not be eaten

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is his claim from the last step: the הקטרה works even on שירים that are חסר.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who takes a handful from the meal offering
intending to eat its remainder outside
or an olive-size of its remainder outside,

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: הַקּוֹמֵץ אֶת הַמִּנְחָה,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chiyya teaches: One who takes a handful from the meal offering,
and he does not teach 'or an olive-size.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא begins proving his own position from Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the הקטרה works on חסר שירים, so they can become פיגול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The difference between our משנה and רבי חייא's version, which leaves out 'או כזית'

steps.title: Why רבי חייא left out 'or an olive-size'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי חייא's case is one where the שירים shrank down to exactly a כזית. In that case, for the later services, 'or a כזית' could not be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he not teach 'or an olive-size'? Isn't it because the case is one where the leftovers shrank and stood at just an olive-size? And since, when it comes to putting the קומץ into a vessel, carrying it, and burning it, he could not teach that phrase...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why רבי חייא left out 'or a כזית'. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שירים are only a כזית, then 'its שירים' and 'a כזית of its שירים' mean the same thing, so 'or a כזית' would add nothing. רבא says this is true at the later services: מתן כלי, הילוך, and הקטרה. So רבי חייא's version must be talking about שירים that became חסר, and it still treats a wrong intent during those services as counting.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftovers became lacking (shrank)
Putting the קומץ into a sacred vessel
Carrying the קומץ to the מזבח
'Isn't it?', a lead-in suggesting the obvious explanation

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא's text is not missing words by accident. רבא reads the omission as a deliberate sign that the case involves שירים that shrank to a כזית.

phrases.english: What is the reason he does not teach 'or an olive-size'?
Is it not a case where the remainder became lacking
and it stood at just an olive-size,
and since, regarding placing it in a vessel,
carrying it, and burning it,
he could not teach it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the textual difference quoted in Step 16 and turns it into evidence.
steps.raayaObject: That שירים which became חסר can still become פיגול through intent during the later services
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא leaves out 'או כזית' because his case has the שירים at exactly a כזית during מתן כלי, הילוך, and הקטרה
